title: T1608.005 — Stage Capabilities - Link Target
subtitle: Interactive walkthrough of Stage Capabilities - Link Target with the technique-specific attack path and defender evidence.
aria: Animated diagram: an attacker stages a fake sign-in page on a fresh domain, wires two redirect domains, sends the link through a hijacked email thread and a mass send, a victim clicks and types credentials, the attacker signs in from another country and adds a hidden inbox rule, and the SOC resets the account and blocks the chain.

nodes.label: Attacker
nodes.tip: The threat actor. Stages the page, wires the redirects, and works the stolen mailbox.

nodes.label: Staged sign-in page
nodes.tip: A convincing clone of the company sign-in page on a 2-day-old domain with a free TLS certificate.

nodes.label: Redirect service
nodes.tip: Two cheap redirect domains that forward to the staged page. Blocked outer hops do not expose the page.

nodes.label: Employee
nodes.tip: A finance employee. Clicks the link inside a trusted vendor thread and types the password.

nodes.label: SOC analyst
nodes.tip: The defender. Joins click telemetry, identity risk, and mailbox audit into one story.

steps.title: Stage the credential page
steps.caption: On a domain registered two days ago the attacker builds a convincing copy of the company sign-in page. A free TLS certificate makes the padlock look trustworthy.
steps.defender: Certificate Transparency logs show the new issuance within minutes - the same early alarm used against T1608.003 certificate staging.

detection.detail: This activity is not visible to the victim yet.

steps.title: Wire the redirect chain
steps.caption: Two throwaway redirect domains are configured to forward to the staged page. If one is blocked, only the cheap outer layer dies - the real page stays live.
steps.defender: Passive DNS shows both redirect domains resolving to the same host that serves the staged page.

steps.title: Hijack a real thread
steps.caption: Using a stolen mailbox, the attacker replies inside a genuine vendor thread and adds the redirect link. The message rides on months of built trust.
steps.defender: The send leaves through the compromised account itself, so it passes every sender check - almost invisible before the click.

steps.title: Mass send the same lure
steps.caption: The identical lure also goes to a purchased address list, one recipient per message, to spread the net wider.
steps.defender: The mail gateway flags single-recipient sends whose links point to domains younger than a week, and rewrites the URLs for time-of-click tracking.

steps.caption: The employee clicks. The link hops through both redirect domains before landing on the staged sign-in page.
steps.defender: Click telemetry records the user, the time, and the full redirect chain - the map needed for blocking later.

steps.title: Credentials are stolen
steps.caption: The employee types the password into the fake page. The relay passes it to the attacker, who signs in from another country within minutes.
steps.defender: The identity provider logs an impossible-travel sign-in: two countries within half an hour, new device, push approved.

steps.title: Hide the tracks
steps.caption: The attacker adds a hidden inbox rule that moves future security messages to the deleted folder, so the victim sees nothing.
steps.defender: The mailbox audit log records the new rule - one of the most reliable post-phishing signals you have.

detection.label: Alert raised
detection.detail: The SOC has enough evidence to open an incident.

steps.title: SOC responds
steps.caption: The SOC resets the password, revokes sessions, removes the rule, blocks the whole chain, and warns the real thread partner.
steps.defender: Historical hunting finds one more clicker who never typed anything - no harm there, but the team now watches that account too.
